message.content: {"schema_version":"teaching-unit.v0.4.0","input_manifest_sha256":"cadbaa228f2d480055e270b42626feb856a1f37a62b94bcbedd5c12d3f7b2a7b","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-ca-class-c:lineage:62","source_registry_sha256":"bc7054e4d59fbb00e9f8cd8f658a743fe5db5406dc1e5275d4d2375fe6e19182","units":[{"unit_id":"sec01-u01","module_id":"sec01-m01","objective_ids":["sec01-u01"],"title":{"text":"What your license allows","fact_ids":["sec01-F01","sec01-F02","sec01-R02"]},"why_how":[{"text":"Knowing what a license allows and which class you need keeps you from driving a vehicle your license does not cover.","fact_ids":["sec01-F01","sec01-F03"]},{"text":"Both licensing tests draw on the handbook, so everything you study here can show up later.","fact_ids":["sec01-F02","sec01-R02"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"Lena holds a Class C license and is offered a job driving a commercial vehicle.","fact_ids":["sec01-F04","sec01-F05"]},"reasoning":{"text":"Her license must match the vehicle, and commercial vehicles call for a different class than Class C.","fact_ids":["sec01-F03","sec01-F05","sec01-R03"]},"result":{"text":"She needs a different license class before she may drive the commercial vehicle.","fact_ids":["sec01-R03"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: thinking one license covers every kind of vehicle.","fact_ids":["sec01-F03"]},"correction":{"text":"The license must match the vehicle; Class C suits most drivers, while commercial vehicles and motorcycles need another class.","fact_ids":["sec01-F04","sec01-F05","sec01-R03"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"Two tests to earn it, the right class to use it.","fact_ids":["sec01-R02","sec01-F03"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"A friend with only a Class C license wants to start riding a motorcycle. Is the Class C license enough?","fact_ids":["sec01-F05","sec01-R03"]},"answer":{"text":"No, a motorcycle calls for a different license class.","fact_ids":["sec01-F05"]},"rationale":{"text":"The license must match the vehicle, and motorcycles are named among the vehicle types that need a class other than Class C.","fact_ids":["sec01-F03","sec01-F05","sec01-R03"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec01-u01-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Your license and the road","fact_ids":["sec01-F01","sec01-F02","sec01-F03","sec01-F04"]},"lines":[{"text":"A license lets you drive on public roads.","fact_ids":["sec01-F01","sec01-F02","sec01-F03","sec01-F04"]},{"text":"Two tests come first.","fact_ids":["sec01-F01","sec01-F02","sec01-F03","sec01-F04"]}],"narration":{"text":"Welcome to the first lesson on the California driver's license. A driver's license is what lets you drive on public roads, and California grants it only after you prove you are ready. In this lesson we look at what the license allows, the two tests you must pass before you get one, and why the license you hold has to match the kind of vehicle you drive. We will also meet Class C, the license most drivers need, and see why other vehicles call for other classes. By the end you will know exactly which license you are working toward and what stands between you and the road.","fact_ids":["sec01-F01","sec01-F02","sec01-F03","sec01-F04"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":43,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u01-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Two separate tests","fact_ids":["sec01-F02","sec01-R02"]},"lines":[{"text":"A knowledge test.","fact_ids":["sec01-F02","sec01-R02"]},{"text":"A behind-the-wheel drive test.","fact_ids":["sec01-F02","sec01-R02"]},{"text":"Both draw on this handbook.","fact_ids":["sec01-F02","sec01-R02"]}],"narration":{"text":"Before California grants you a driver's license, you must pass two different tests. The first is a knowledge test, and the second is a behind-the-wheel drive test. Both of them are drawn from the handbook, which means every later section you study is material you may be tested on. Passing the knowledge test alone does not finish the job, and the drive test is not a formality you can skip. Think of them as two separate gates on the same path, one checking what you know and the other checking how you drive. Keep that picture in mind as you move through the rest of the course.","fact_ids":["sec01-F02","sec01-R02"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":43,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u01-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Matching license to vehicle","fact_ids":["sec01-F03","sec01-F04","sec01-F05","sec01-F14"]},"lines":[{"text":"Your license must match the vehicle.","fact_ids":["sec01-F03","sec01-F04","sec01-F05","sec01-F14"]},{"text":"Most drivers need Class C.","fact_ids":["sec01-F03","sec01-F04","sec01-F05","sec01-F14"]},{"text":"Other vehicles need other classes.","fact_ids":["sec01-F03","sec01-F04","sec01-F05","sec01-F14"]}],"narration":{"text":"Your license must match the kind of vehicle you drive. For most people that means a noncommercial Class C driver's license, the license this course prepares you for. Driving a commercial vehicle, a motorcycle, or some other vehicle type calls for a different license class. So the question is never only whether you have a license, but whether you have the right class of license for the vehicle in front of you. If you are not sure which vehicles a Class C license covers, the DMV posts those details on its driver's license web pages, and that is the place to check before you get behind the wheel.","fact_ids":["sec01-F03","sec01-F04","sec01-F05","sec01-F14"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":43,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u01-s4","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"A worked example","fact_ids":["sec01-F03","sec01-F04","sec01-F05","sec01-R03"]},"lines":[{"text":"Lena holds a Class C license.","fact_ids":["sec01-F03","sec01-F04","sec01-F05","sec01-R03"]},{"text":"She is offered a commercial driving job.","fact_ids":["sec01-F03","sec01-F04","sec01-F05","sec01-R03"]},{"text":"She needs a different class first.","fact_ids":["sec01-F03","sec01-F04","sec01-F05","sec01-R03"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a worked example. Lena holds a Class C license and is offered a job driving a commercial vehicle. Can she simply start? Walk through the rules. Her license must match the kind of vehicle she drives. Class C is the noncommercial license most drivers need, and commercial vehicles are named among the vehicle types that call for a different license class. So the answer is no, not yet. Before she drives that commercial vehicle, Lena needs the license class that covers it. The same reasoning applies to a motorcycle or any other vehicle type outside Class C.","fact_ids":["sec01-F03","sec01-F04","sec01-F05","sec01-R03"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u01-s5","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"One license for everything?","fact_ids":["sec01-F03","sec01-F04","sec01-F05","sec01-R03"]},"lines":[{"text":"Trap: one license covers every vehicle.","fact_ids":["sec01-F03","sec01-F04","sec01-F05","sec01-R03"]},{"text":"Truth: the class must match the vehicle.","fact_ids":["sec01-F03","sec01-F04","sec01-F05","sec01-R03"]}],"narration":{"text":"A common mistake is thinking that once you have a driver's license, you can drive any vehicle at all. That is not how licensing works. Your license must match the kind of vehicle you drive. Class C is the noncommercial license that most drivers need, but commercial vehicles, motorcycles, and other vehicle types each call for a different class. So a driver who holds only Class C and climbs onto a motorcycle is not covered by that license. When a question describes a vehicle, always ask which class it needs before you decide whether the driver may operate it.","fact_ids":["sec01-F03","sec01-F04","sec01-F05","sec01-R03"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u01-s6","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check your understanding","fact_ids":["sec01-F05","sec01-R03","sec01-F03"]},"lines":[{"text":"A Class C driver wants to ride a motorcycle.","fact_ids":["sec01-F05","sec01-R03","sec01-F03"]},{"text":"Is Class C enough?","fact_ids":["sec01-F05","sec01-R03","sec01-F03"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: a friend has only a Class C license and wants to start riding a motorcycle. Is the Class C license enough? Decide before you go on. The answer is no. Motorcycles are named among the vehicle types that call for a different license class, and your license must match the vehicle you drive. Class C is the noncommercial license most drivers need for everyday driving, but it is not the class for a motorcycle. If you got this right, you have the core idea of license classes. If not, go back over the matching rule and the list of vehicles that need another class.","fact_ids":["sec01-F05","sec01-R03","sec01-F03"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":44,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u01-s7","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Ready for the next step","fact_ids":["sec01-F01","sec01-F02","sec01-R02","sec01-F04","sec01-F05","sec01-F14"]},"lines":[{"text":"License means public roads.","fact_ids":["sec01-F01","sec01-F02","sec01-R02","sec01-F04","sec01-F05","sec01-F14"]},{"text":"Two tests, then the right class.","fact_ids":["sec01-F01","sec01-F02","sec01-R02","sec01-F04","sec01-F05","sec01-F14"]}],"narration":{"text":"Let us pull this lesson together. A California driver's license lets you drive on public roads. To earn it, you must pass both a knowledge test and a behind-the-wheel drive test, and both draw on the handbook. Once you have it, your license must match the vehicle you drive. Most drivers need a noncommercial Class C license, while commercial vehicles, motorcycles, and other vehicle types call for a different class. When you want details on what Class C covers, the DMV driver's license pages hold them. apart.","fact_ids":["sec01-F06","sec01-R04","sec01-R05"]}],"narration":{"text":"This lesson is about REAL ID and the other designations a California card can carry. Starting in May of twenty twenty-five, a driver's license or ID card must be REAL ID compliant to board domestic flights, and REAL ID matters in a few other places too. We will list the three kinds of access REAL ID unlocks, see where to learn about applying, and then separate REAL ID from two other designations, the Veteran designation and organ donor status. These are easy to blur together, so we will keep each one in its own box and look at what it actually does for you.","fact_ids":["sec01-F06","sec01-R04","sec01-R05"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":42,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u02-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Three doors for REAL ID","fact_ids":["sec01-F06","sec01-F07","sec01-F08","sec01-F15","sec01-R04"]},"lines":[{"text":"Domestic flights.","fact_ids":["sec01-F06","sec01-F07","sec01-F08","sec01-F15","sec01-R04"]},{"text":"Military bases.","fact_ids":["sec01-F06","sec01-F07","sec01-F08","sec01-F15","sec01-R04"]},{"text":"Most federal facilities.","fact_ids":["sec01-F06","sec01-F07","sec01-F08","sec01-F15","sec01-R04"]}],"narration":{"text":"REAL ID compliance unlocks three separate doors. First, starting in May of twenty twenty-five, a license or ID card must be REAL ID compliant to board domestic flights. Second, a REAL ID is also needed to enter military bases. Third, most federal facilities likewise require a REAL ID for entry. Learners often remember the airport and forget the other two, so practice naming all three together. If you want to learn how to apply for a REAL ID, the DMV keeps a page dedicated to REAL ID applications, separate from its other license and ID card pages.","fact_ids":["sec01-F06","sec01-F07","sec01-F08","sec01-F15","sec01-R04"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u02-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Veteran and donor markings","fact_ids":["sec01-F10","sec01-F11","sec01-R05"]},"lines":[{"text":"Veteran designation has its own page.","fact_ids":["sec01-F10","sec01-F11","sec01-R05"]},{"text":"Donor information has its own website.","fact_ids":["sec01-F10","sec01-F11","sec01-R05"]}],"narration":{"text":"A card can carry other designations that have nothing to do with REAL ID. The requirements and benefits of a Veteran designation are explained on the DMV veterans page. Information about becoming an organ and tissue donor is available from Donate Life California. Each of these is its own designation with its own source of information. Neither one makes a card REAL ID compliant, and REAL ID does not make you a veteran or a donor. Keep the three separate: REAL ID for federally controlled access, the Veteran designation for its own requirements and benefits, and donor status recorded on its own.","fact_ids":["sec01-F10","sec01-F11","sec01-R05"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":41,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u02-s4","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Designations are not interchangeable","fact_ids":["sec01-R05","sec01-F06","sec01-F11","sec01-F10"]},"lines":[{"text":"Trap: any special marking equals REAL ID.","fact_ids":["sec01-R05","sec01-F06","sec01-F11","sec01-F10"]},{"text":"Truth: each designation stands alone.","fact_ids":["sec01-R05","sec01-F06","sec01-F11","sec01-F10"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a trap worth spotting. Some people assume that any special marking on a card, such as a Veteran designation or organ donor status, also makes the card good for flights or federal buildings. It does not. REAL ID governs federally controlled access, which means domestic flights, military bases, and most federal facilities. The Veteran designation carries its own requirements and benefits, and organ donor status is recorded separately. When a question asks what lets you board a domestic flight, the answer is REAL ID compliance, not the Veteran designation and not the donor marking.","fact_ids":["sec01-R05","sec01-F06","sec01-F11","sec01-F10"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u02-s5","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check your understanding","fact_ids":["sec01-R04","sec01-F06","sec01-F07","sec01-F08"]},"lines":[{"text":"Name the three REAL ID uses.","fact_ids":["sec01-R04","sec01-F06","sec01-F07","sec01-F08"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: name the three kinds of access that a REAL ID compliant card unlocks. Try to list all three before you continue. The answer is boarding domestic flights, entering military bases, and entering most federal facilities. The handbook lists these as separate uses, so a card that is not REAL ID compliant can be turned away at any of them. If you named only the airport, add the military base and the federal facility to your memory list. Picture three doors in a row, a flight gate, a base entrance, and a federal building, all asking for the same card.","fact_ids":["sec01-R04","sec01-F06","sec01-F07","sec01-F08"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":42,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u02-s6","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Keep the boxes separate","fact_ids":["sec01-R04","sec01-F15","sec01-F11","sec01-F10","sec01-R05","sec01-F08"]},"lines":[{"text":"REAL ID: flights, bases, federal buildings.","fact_ids":["sec01-R04","sec01-F15","sec01-F11","sec01-F10","sec01-R05","sec01-F08"]},{"text":"Veteran and donor: separate designations.","fact_ids":["sec01-R04","sec01-F15","sec01-F11","sec01-F10","sec01-R05","sec01-F08"]}],"narration":{"text":"To wrap up, REAL ID compliance unlocks three doors: boarding domestic flights starting in May of twenty twenty-five, entering military bases, and entering most federal facilities. The DMV has a dedicated REAL ID page for learning how to apply. Two other designations stand apart from REAL ID. The Veteran designation has its own requirements and benefits, explained on the DMV veterans page, and organ and tissue donor information comes from Donate Life California. Keep each designation in its own box and you will not confuse them. Next, we look at who can get a license and how ID cards work.","fact_ids":["sec01-R04","sec01-F15","sec01-F11","sec01-F10","sec01-R05","sec01-F08"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"}]},{"unit_id":"sec01-u03","module_id":"sec01-m03","objective_ids":["sec01-u03"],"title":{"text":"Eligibility and ID cards","fact_ids":["sec01-F09","sec01-F12","sec01-F13"]},"why_how":[{"text":"Knowing that an ID card never permits driving keeps you from relying on the wrong card behind the wheel.","fact_ids":["sec01-F12","sec01-R01"]},{"text":"Bringing the three required proofs saves a wasted trip when you apply for an ID card.","fact_ids":["sec01-F13","sec01-R06"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"Ana, a California resident, wants an ID card and asks what to bring and whether her immigration status matters.","fact_ids":["sec01-F09","sec01-F13"]},"reasoning":{"text":"Immigration status never blocks a license, but an ID card applicant must show an identity document, residency documents, and a social security number.","fact_ids":["sec01-R07","sec01-F13"]},"result":{"text":"Ana gathers all three proofs; her status is not a barrier to a license, and residency documents are part of the ID card proofs.","fact_ids":["sec01-R06","sec01-R07"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: thinking an ID card lets you drive as long as you carry it.","fact_ids":["sec01-F12","sec01-R01"]},"correction":{"text":"A license grants the privilege of driving on public roads, while an ID card only proves identity and never permits driving.","fact_ids":["sec01-R01","sec01-F01"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"License drives, ID identifies.","fact_ids":["sec01-R01"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"Does holding a California ID card allow you to drive on public roads?","fact_ids":["sec01-R01","sec01-F12"]},"answer":{"text":"No, an ID card only proves identity and never permits driving.","fact_ids":["sec01-R01","sec01-F12"]},"rationale":{"text":"Driving requires a license; the ID card exists to prove identity for eligible people of any age.","fact_ids":["sec01-R01","sec01-F12"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec01-u03-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Who can get a card","fact_ids":["sec01-F09","sec01-F12","sec01-R01"]},"lines":[{"text":"Every resident can get a license.","fact_ids":["sec01-F09","sec01-F12","sec01-R01"]},{"text":"ID cards prove identity.","fact_ids":["sec01-F09","sec01-F12","sec01-R01"]}],"narration":{"text":"This lesson covers who can get a California driver's license and how ID cards fit in. California issues driver's licenses to every resident, no matter their immigration status. Alongside licenses, the state offers identification cards to eligible people of any age, but those cards serve a different purpose. We will see what an ID card does and does not allow, the three proofs an ID card applicant must bring, and where on the DMV website each of these topics lives. These rules are short, but they are often mixed up, so we will compare them side by side.","fact_ids":["sec01-F09","sec01-F12","sec01-R01"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u03-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Licenses for every resident","fact_ids":["sec01-F09","sec01-R07","sec01-F13"]},"lines":[{"text":"Every resident may get a license.","fact_ids":["sec01-F09","sec01-R07","sec01-F13"]},{"text":"Immigration status is not a barrier.","fact_ids":["sec01-F09","sec01-R07","sec01-F13"]}],"narration":{"text":"California issues driver's licenses to every resident, no matter their immigration status. That means immigration status is never the reason a resident is turned away from a license. Keep this separate from the ID card rules you will meet next. An ID card applicant still has to show residency documents as one of the required proofs, so residency is something you prove on paper even though immigration status does not block a license. Holding both ideas at once is the hard part of this lesson: status is not a barrier to the license, and residency documents are still part of the ID card application.","fact_ids":["sec01-F09","sec01-R07","sec01-F13"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":42,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u03-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"What an ID card does","fact_ids":["sec01-F12","sec01-R01","sec01-F01"]},"lines":[{"text":"Proves identity for any age.","fact_ids":["sec01-F12","sec01-R01","sec01-F01"]},{"text":"Never authorizes driving.","fact_ids":["sec01-F12","sec01-R01","sec01-F01"]}],"narration":{"text":"Identification cards go to eligible people of any age, and their job is to prove identity. They never authorize driving. This is the key contrast of the section. A driver's license grants the privilege of driving on public roads, while an ID card only proves who you are. Carrying an ID card in your pocket does not let you drive, no matter how long you have held it. If someone needs to drive, they need a license of the right class. If someone only needs to prove their identity, an ID card does that job for eligible people of every age.","fact_ids":["sec01-F12","sec01-R01","sec01-F01"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u03-s4","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Three proofs for an ID","fact_ids":["sec01-F13","sec01-R06","sec01-F16"]},"lines":[{"text":"An identity document.","fact_ids":["sec01-F13","sec01-R06","sec01-F16"]},{"text":"Residency documents.","fact_ids":["sec01-F13","sec01-R06","sec01-F16"]},{"text":"A social security number.","fact_ids":["sec01-F13","sec01-R06","sec01-F16"]}],"narration":{"text":"An ID card applicant must show three things: an identity document, residency documents, and a social security number. ID cards are open to eligible people of any age, yet every applicant still needs all three proofs. A good way to remember them is identity, residency, and social security, in that order. If you arrive with only one or two, the application is not complete. The DMV keeps a page for ID card applications that also covers acceptable documents and the reduced-fee, no-fee, and senior ID card options, so that is the place to check before you go.","fact_ids":["sec01-F13","sec01-R06","sec01-F16"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u03-s5","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Status and residency","fact_ids":["sec01-R07","sec01-F09","sec01-F13"]},"lines":[{"text":"Trap: status and residency are the same rule.","fact_ids":["sec01-R07","sec01-F09","sec01-F13"]},{"text":"Truth: one never blocks, one is required.","fact_ids":["sec01-R07","sec01-F09","sec01-F13"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is the hardest trap in this section. People hear that immigration status never blocks a California license and assume no documents about where they live are needed for anything. That mixes up two different rules. Immigration status never blocks a license. But an ID card applicant must still show residency documents, along with an identity document and a social security number. So residency documents are a required ID card proof, even though immigration status is not a barrier to the license. When a question pairs these ideas, check which one it is really asking about before you choose.","fact_ids":["sec01-R07","sec01-F09","sec01-F13"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u03-s6","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Where to look online","fact_ids":["sec01-R08","sec01-F14","sec01-F15","sec01-F11","sec01-F16"]},"lines":[{"text":"Each topic has its own DMV page.","fact_ids":["sec01-R08","sec01-F14","sec01-F15","sec01-F11","sec01-F16"]},{"text":"License, REAL ID, veterans, ID cards.","fact_ids":["sec01-R08","sec01-F14","sec01-F15","sec01-F11","sec01-F16"]}],"narration":{"text":"Each topic in this section has its own place on the DMV website. Details of which vehicles a Class C license covers sit under the driver's license pages. Applying for a REAL ID has its own page.
